DrawingPlanes__Description: Configuration for the Drawing Planes system - the planes that show, in the 3D view, where each floor plan is cut and where each elevation or section is taken from. A plane carries its drawing's name and its own colour, can be switched on alone or with all the others, dragged along its own normal, snapped to a world grid and sent to a picked building face. It is an authoring aid: it is never drawn into a drawing, a sheet, a thumbnail or an export. All distance values are integer millimetres and are converted to Three.js units in code.

DrawingPlanes__Snap__Config.DrawingPlanes__Snap__Description: The snap grid. The ABSOLUTE position of a plane along its own normal is snapped to a multiple of the increment, measured from the world origin - never the distance dragged - so a plane that started off the grid lands on it and every plane in the model shares one grid. The increments are the steps the panel's stepper moves through; the default must be one of them. The author's last choice is kept in the browser and overrides these defaults.

DrawingPlanes__Bounds__Config.DrawingPlanes__Bounds__Description: How large a plane is drawn. It is sized from the BUILDING alone: a category counts as building when its key holds one of the building tokens. The landscape is never measured - on a real project it is a slab tens of metres across and would make every plane the size of the site. It is used for one thing only: a vertical plane's bottom edge sits GroundLiftMm above the highest point where the plane meets an upward face of a ground category, inside the building's span. The overshoot is how far a plane runs past the building on each side, and is what gives the corner grips room to be grabbed clear of the building's outline: the larger of OvershootMm and OvershootFraction of the building's longer horizontal side.

DrawingPlanes__Appearance__Config.DrawingPlanes__Appearance__Description: What a plane looks like. Each plane takes one colour from the palette for its face, outline, grips, label and arrows; the colour is chosen by the number in the record's own id, so deleting a drawing never recolours the others, and floor plans start PlanPaletteOffset places along so a plan and an elevation with the same number differ. Sizes are fractions of the building's longer horizontal side, held between a minimum and a maximum in millimetres, so the grips read the same on a garden room and on a full house. The ghost outline is the same outline drawn without depth testing, so a plane can be followed where the building hides it.

DrawingPlanes__Grip__Config.DrawingPlanes__Grip__Description: Dragging and picking. A drag is solved as the point on the plane's own normal closest to the pointer ray, so a plane never slides sideways. When that normal points almost straight at the camera the solve turns a pixel into metres, so inside MinAxisAngleDeg of the view direction the plane holds still and the readout asks for a better angle. Each drag step can recut a live section, which is the expensive part, so the live callback is throttled. The click threshold is in pixels: a press that travels further was an orbit, not a click.

DrawingPlanes__Labels__Config.DrawingPlanes__Labels__Description: User-facing wording for the Drawing Planes bar, the per-row controls and the toasts.
DrawingPlanes__Labels__Config.DrawingPlanes__Labels__SnapOnHint: Planes land on a {increment} mm grid measured from the model origin. Click to move them freely.
DrawingPlanes__Labels__Config.DrawingPlanes__Labels__SnapOffHint: Planes move freely, to the millimetre. Click to snap them to a {increment} mm grid.
DrawingPlanes__Labels__Config.DrawingPlanes__Labels__ShowPlaneHint: Show this drawing's plane in the 3D view. Drag it by a corner grip or its name.
DrawingPlanes__Labels__Config.DrawingPlanes__Labels__MoveToFaceHint: Then click a building face: the plane keeps its direction and moves to that face, on the snap grid.
DrawingPlanes__Labels__Config.DrawingPlanes__Labels__AimAtFaceHint: Then click a wall: the elevation turns to face that wall square on, and its plane moves to it.
DrawingPlanes__Labels__Config.DrawingPlanes__Labels__PickingHint: Click a building face in the 3D view. Drag to orbit first if you need to. Escape cancels.
DrawingPlanes__Labels__Config.DrawingPlanes__Labels__PickNeeds3dMessag: Leave the drawing first - a face is picked in the 3D view.
DrawingPlanes__Labels__Config.DrawingPlanes__Labels__NoModelMessage: Load a model before showing drawing planes.
DrawingPlanes__Labels__Config.DrawingPlanes__Labels__BetterAngleHint: orbit round - this plane is facing you
DrawingPlanes__Labels__Config.DrawingPlanes__Labels__BarNote: Drag a plane by a corner grip or its name; once selected, by its whole face. Planes never appear in a drawing, a sheet or an export.
